claims: A rate-limited CodeRabbit consumes the one-per-head request and permanently suppresses retry — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:786`: the terminal-check trigger fires precisely in the rate-limited case, so the PR merges with no exact-head CodeRabbit review and the signal stuck at `requested`, with no state permitting a retry
The ADR notes `@coderabbitai rate limit` reports remaining capacity without consuming a review (`docs/adr/0066...md:220`), but the procedure never checks it

The canonical JSON contract sample was not updated — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:282` and `:305`: the sample output block still shows only `codexReviewSignal` in `gates` (lines 282-287) and only `"codexReviewSignal": "in_flight"` at top level (line 305), omitting `codeRabbitReviewSignal`

Redundant timestamp clause can only produce a false `stale` — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:776-779`: the `isCurrentSignal` `&&` clause adds no discrimination and, if `headUpdatedAt` resolves later than the comment, degrades a valid same-head request to `stale`, telling the agent to post a duplicate `@coderabbitai review`

The config test traded an invariant for a literal — `scripts/coderabbit-config.test.mjs:121-125`: the replacement asserts `auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits === 5` against `EXPECTED_CONFIG`, duplicating the pin test at line 118 and no longer expressing any policy bound, so a future change to 20 fails with a bare equality mismatch

Case-sensitivity asymmetry — `pr-ready-state-core.mjs:443` vs `:658`: `isCodeRabbitFinalHeadReviewRequestBody` lowercases both sides of the OID comparison while `isCurrentReviewSignal` uses strict `===` on `reviewCommitOid(review)`
`docs/adr/0066...md:281-283`: the ADR frames 5 as resolving the friction when it resolves roughly a third of the observed cases — the prose reads stronger than the data supports

judge_reasoning.3829654081: The review never raises file size, the 600-line cap, or splitting pr-ready-state-core.mjs; its findings there are about logic, not structure.
judge_reasoning.3829659544: Review finding 2 states the doc's canonical sample JSON still shows only codexReviewSignal in gates and omits the newly documented codeRabbitReviewSignal — same defect.
judge_reasoning.3829659546: No mention of ordering the CodeRabbit closeout rule relative to the feedback-state/ready-state projection pair, or of aligning the workflow with the ship mirrors.
judge_reasoning.3829659550: Review finding 3 touches the same lines but argues the opposite (drop the timestamp clause as redundant); it never identifies that a null currentHeadOid lets the classifier return requested/reviewed without an exact head match.

1.why: Verified at pr-ready-state-core.mjs:786 that `requested` is terminal with fallbackAction `wait` and docs forbid re-posting for the same head; this is the already-known Major functional-correctness defect anchored at core:783 / docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:408 in the same requested/stale block and all-clear step.

2.why: ADR line 220 does say `@coderabbitai rate limit` reports capacity without consuming a review, and no skill/doc procedure calls it — but that is an enhancement suggestion, not a defect in the added code or procedure.

3.why: docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md sample JSON at 282-287 and 305 still lists only codexReviewSignal in `gates` and at top level, while the same file's field expectations (351-355) and the code (terminalGates/summarizeReadyState) now emit codeRabbitReviewSignal — the canonical contract sample is out of sync.

4.why: isCodeRabbitFinalHeadReviewRequestBody returns true when currentHeadOid is null (line 442), so the isCurrentSignal clause at 778 is the only discriminator in that case; and headUpdatedAt is the head commit's timeline timestamp min'd with observedAt (pr-ready-state.mjs:589-618), which cannot postdate a comment carrying that head's OID, so the claimed false `stale` is unreachable.

5.why: coderabbit-config.test.mjs:121-125 does assert the literal 5 against EXPECTED_CONFIG, but line 118 is the negative-control added-key assertion (not a pin of 5), and the deepEqual pin at line 96 still ties the yaml to that constant — a test-style preference about expressing a bound, not a defect.

6.why: Confirmed the asymmetry (line 443 lowercases both sides; line 658 uses `===`), but line 658 is pre-existing code shared with the codex path and GitHub only returns lowercase 40-hex OIDs, so no failure is named — a consistency nit.

7.why: ADR 277-283 states the sample (16/29 paused, six with 2-4 commits) and 281-283 only claims 5 'preserves the burst guard without treating one normal fix round as active development'; the objection is a subjective prose-strength critique with no concrete error.
